findings.where: 'Median close time across customer teams…' caption, tile 01
findings.evidence: Pixel sample on image.png: darkest text pixel rgb(119,118,110) on rgb(238,237,228), about 3.9:1 at roughly 13px. The source note for the page's main claim is the least legible text on it.
findings.before: light grey caption on beige band

findings.where: secondary grey text: 'Built for finance teams of 3 to 30', 'Lines matched', '3 to 8 people', 'per month', testimonial attribution
findings.evidence: Pixel samples give the darkest pixel at rgb(116-121,114-121,110-119) on near-white, 4.3-4.4:1. Anti-aliasing means this is a best case; at 13-14px these fail 4.5:1 by a small margin.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum); estimate from a raster, confirm on the live page.

findings.evidence: 'Amount differs' / 'Not in ledger' are brown-orange on pale orange (sample about 4.5:1, borderline) at about 12px; state is also given in words and the row tint, so colour is not the only cue.
findings.after: Darken pill text to about #7a4a1f and set it at 13px or more.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 Contrast and 1.4.1 Use of Color (passes on words).

strengths: State is never colour-only: every pill carries a word and the bar chart labels both bars with text and values.
Text on the dark green bands samples at 7.7-8.7:1.
not_investigated: image-only item: alt text, link purpose, focus order, keyboard, landmarks, headings, forms, reflow at 320px and motion cannot be checked from a static image
contrast figures are raster estimates from anti-aliased glyphs, not computed from CSS
